claims.title: The Cradle of Humankind
claims.summary: The Sterkfontein and Swartkrans caves preserve hominin fossils spanning millions of years, including Mrs Ples and Little Foot, marking southern Africa as a key site of human origins; the area was inscribed by UNESCO in 1999.

sources.label: Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa

claims.title: San and Khoekhoe of the subcontinent
claims.summary: The San, hunter-gatherers present for tens of thousands of years, were joined around two thousand years ago by the herding Khoekhoe, together forming the long-established Khoisan societies of the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-2000bce-san-and-khoekhoe-of-the-subcontinent, claim TL:ZAF:event:2000bce:san-and-khoekhoe-of-the-subcontinent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bantu-speaking farmers spread south
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking communities bringing iron-working, cattle and cultivated crops settled the eastern half of southern Africa, ancestors of the region's Nguni, Sotho-Tswana, Venda and Tsonga peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-300-bantu-speaking-farmers-spread-south, claim TL:ZAF:event:300:bantu-speaking-farmers-spread-south, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The kingdom of Mapungubwe
claims.summary: Near the Limpopo, Mapungubwe rose as southern Africa's first state-level society, trading gold and ivory to the Indian Ocean coast and producing famed gold artefacts before its decline around 1300.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1220-the-kingdom-of-mapungubwe, claim TL:ZAF:event:1220:the-kingdom-of-mapungubwe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Van Riebeeck founds the Cape station
claims.summary: Jan van Riebeeck landed at Table Bay and established a Dutch East India Company refreshment station, the beginning of permanent European settlement in South Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1652-van-riebeeck-founds-the-cape-station, claim TL:ZAF:event:1652:van-riebeeck-founds-the-cape-station, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavery at the Cape
claims.summary: The Company began importing enslaved people from Madagascar, East Africa, India and the Indonesian archipelago, founding a slave society whose labour underpinned the colony for nearly two centuries.

sources.label: History of slavery and early colonisation in South Africa

claims.title: Smallpox devastates the Khoekhoe
claims.summary: A smallpox epidemic introduced by passing ships killed great numbers of Khoekhoe, accelerating the loss of their land, herds and independence as the colony expanded.

sources.label: History of slavery and early colonisation in South Africa

claims.title: First Cape Frontier War
claims.summary: As trekboers reached the Great Fish River they clashed with the Xhosa, beginning a century-long series of frontier wars along the colony's eastern edge.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1779-first-cape-frontier-war, claim TL:ZAF:event:1779:first-cape-frontier-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain seizes the Cape
claims.summary: British forces occupied the Cape Colony during the Napoleonic Wars, beginning lasting British rule confirmed by the Congress of Vienna in 1815.

sources.label: History of slavery and early colonisation in South Africa

claims.title: Rise of the Zulu kingdom and the Mfecane
claims.summary: Shaka built the Zulu into a powerful centralised kingdom with a reorganised army; the wars and migrations of the Mfecane reshaped the political map of southern Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1816-rise-of-the-zulu-kingdom-and-the-mfecane, claim TL:ZAF:event:1816:rise-of-the-zulu-kingdom-and-the-mfecane, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of slavery at the Cape
claims.summary: Slavery was abolished across the British Empire, freeing enslaved people at the Cape and deepening Boer discontent that helped spark the Great Trek.

sources.label: History of slavery and early colonisation in South Africa

claims.title: The Great Trek
claims.summary: Thousands of Voortrekkers left the Cape Colony for the interior, seeking independence from British rule and founding new Boer communities on lands occupied by African peoples.

sources.label: Origins of the Battle of Blood River 1838

claims.title: Battle of Blood River
claims.summary: A Voortrekker commando under Andries Pretorius defeated a large Zulu army at the Ncome (Blood) River, a battle long mythologised in Afrikaner nationalism and preceding the rise of Boer republics.

sources.label: Origins of the Battle of Blood River 1838

claims.title: Diamonds discovered at Kimberley
claims.summary: The discovery of diamonds near the Vaal and Orange rivers triggered a rush to Kimberley, beginning the mineral revolution and drawing capital and migrant labour into the region.

sources.label: South Africa: Diamonds, gold and imperialist intervention (1870–1902)

claims.title: Gold found on the Witwatersrand
claims.summary: The discovery of the world's largest goldfield on the Witwatersrand created Johannesburg, transformed the Transvaal's wealth, and entrenched a segregated migrant-labour system.

sources.label: South Africa: Diamonds, gold and imperialist intervention (1870–1902)
Grade 8 – Topic 2 – The Mineral Revolution in South Africa

claims.title: The South African War
claims.summary: War between Britain and the Boer republics featured guerrilla campaigns and British concentration camps in which tens of thousands of Boer and Black civilians died.

claims.title: Treaty of Vereeniging
claims.summary: The peace signed at Pretoria ended the South African War, bringing the Transvaal and Orange Free State under British sovereignty with promises of eventual self-government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1902-treaty-of-vereeniging, claim TL:ZAF:event:1902:treaty-of-vereeniging, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of South Africa
claims.summary: The four British colonies were united into the self-governing Union of South Africa under the South Africa Act, a white-controlled state that excluded the Black majority from political power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1910-union-of-south-africa, claim TL:ZAF:event:1910:union-of-south-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: National Party institutes apartheid
claims.summary: The National Party won the 1948 election and began enacting apartheid, including the Population Registration Act and Group Areas Act of 1950, codifying racial classification, segregation and forced removals.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1948-national-party-institutes-apartheid, claim TL:ZAF:event:1948:national-party-institutes-apartheid, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sharpeville massacre
claims.summary: Police fired on a peaceful anti-pass-law protest at Sharpeville, killing at least 69 people and wounding scores more; the atrocity drew global condemnation and led to the banning of the ANC and PAC.

claims.title: Rivonia Trial imprisons Mandela
claims.summary: Nelson Mandela and fellow leaders of the ANC's armed wing were convicted of sabotage and sentenced to life imprisonment, beginning Mandela's 27 years behind bars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1964-rivonia-trial-imprisons-mandela, claim TL:ZAF:event:1964:rivonia-trial-imprisons-mandela, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Soweto uprising
claims.summary: Student protests against compulsory instruction in Afrikaans were met with police gunfire in Soweto, killing many, including children, and igniting nationwide resistance.

sources.label: Grade 8 – Topic 2 – The Mineral Revolution in South Africa

claims.title: Mandela freed and the ANC unbanned
claims.summary: President F. W. de Klerk unbanned the ANC, PAC and other organisations and released Nelson Mandela from prison, opening the way to negotiations that would dismantle apartheid.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1990-mandela-freed-and-the-anc-unbanned, claim TL:ZAF:event:1990:mandela-freed-and-the-anc-unbanned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First democratic election
claims.summary: South Africans of all races voted together for the first time; the ANC won about 62.65 percent of the vote on an 86.9 percent turnout, ending apartheid rule. The main polling day, 27 April, is marked as Freedom Day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1994-first-democratic-election, claim TL:ZAF:event:1994:first-democratic-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mandela inaugurated as president
claims.summary: Nelson Mandela was sworn in as the first president of a democratic South Africa, leading a Government of National Unity and symbolising reconciliation across the country's racial divide.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Africa: From the cradle of humankind and the early San, Khoekhoe and Bantu-speaking kingdoms, through Dutch and British colonisation, the trauma of apartheid, and the birth of a non-racial democracy in 1994.", terralore.co/country/ZAF/chronicle#ev-1994-mandela-inaugurated-as-president, claim TL:ZAF:event:1994:mandela-inaugurated-as-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission
claims.summary: Chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the TRC began public hearings into apartheid-era human rights abuses, offering conditional amnesty in exchange for full disclosure as a model of transitional justice.

sources.label: South Africa Truth and Reconciliation Commission (1996–2002)

claims.title: A new Constitution
claims.summary: South Africa's final Constitution, with its justiciable Bill of Rights, was signed into law in 1996 and took effect in February 1997, widely regarded as among the most progressive in the world.

sources.label: Mandela signs SA Constitution into law

claims.title: ANC loses its majority
claims.summary: In the 2024 general election the ANC lost the outright parliamentary majority it had held since 1994, leading to a multiparty government of national unity and a new phase of coalition politics.
